about: I am interested in how people recognize written words and build meaning in context. My research combines behavioral experiments, EEG/ERP methods, and computational measures of language predictability.
background: My academic background is in Linguistics and Applied Linguistics at Sichuan University, where my master’s research was supervised by Dr. Feng Gu.

research.title: Coercion and predictability in Mandarin
research.text: I investigate coercion in Mandarin adverb–noun constructions, bringing together EEG, behavioral norms, and computational measures of predictability.
contributions: Designed the EEG experiment and stimuli, recruited 60 participants, and conducted EEG data collection.
Collected completion norms and semantic ratings, computed LLM surprisal, and modeled trial-level EEG responses using regression-based ERP estimation (rERP).
research.methods: EEG · Completion norms · LLM surprisal · rERP

research.title: Object size and semantic processing
research.text: This project examined cognitive and neural differences in processing words referring to small and large objects.
contributions: Recruited 228 participants across the behavioral and EEG experiments and organized subjective semantic ratings.
Preprocessed EEG data in MATLAB and contributed to multivariate pattern analysis using MVPA-Light.

research.title: Orthographic processing and the ND250
research.text: This project investigated the functional interpretation of the ND250 response by comparing handwritten and printed words.
contributions: Contributed to the 2 × 2 experimental design, prepared 300 stimuli, and independently conducted the EEG experiment after recruiting 30 participants.
Performed univariate ND250 analyses and exploratory mass-univariate analyses with false discovery rate correction.
